title: Benign prostatic hyperplasia and male lower urinary tract symptoms
subject: urology
setting: Primary care, urology outpatient, emergency department
summary: Assess male LUTS with history, IPSS, urinalysis, DRE, post-void residual and counselled PSA. Offer watchful waiting for mild symptoms, an alpha-blocker for bothersome moderate to severe LUTS, add a 5-ARI when the prostate is enlarged, and refer for surgery for retention, renal impairment, recurrent UTI, stones or haematuria.

sections.title: Recognise and assess
items: LUTS: voiding (weak stream, hesitancy, straining, incomplete emptying), storage (frequency, urgency, nocturia, urge incontinence) and post-micturition dribble. Causes include prostatic obstruction, overactive bladder, nocturnal polyuria, stricture, stones, infection, bladder cancer and neurological disease.
Score with the IPSS (0 to 7 mild, 8 to 19 moderate, 20 to 35 severe) plus the quality-of-life (bother) question, and repeat it to judge response.
Examine for a palpable bladder, do a DRE (size, nodules, tenderness) and a focused neurological examination; urinalysis in every man.
Bladder diary for at least 3 days when storage symptoms or nocturia predominate (identifies nocturnal polyuria).

sections.title: Investigations
items: PSA: counsel first; measure it if a prostate cancer diagnosis would change management or if it guides treatment (PSA above 1.5 ng/mL suggests an enlarged prostate).
Post-void residual (bladder scan) in all men; uroflowmetry before medical or invasive treatment (EAU).
Creatinine and upper tract ultrasound if renal impairment is suspected, residual is large, or surgery is planned. Prostate imaging when it helps drug choice or before surgery.
Urodynamics only in selected men before invasive treatment: voided volume under 150 mL, Qmax above 10 mL/s, post-void residual above 300 mL, age under 50 or over 80, or previous failed treatment.
Refer for suspicious DRE, raised PSA, visible haematuria, abnormal urinalysis or suspected neurological disease.

sections.title: Conservative and drug treatment
items: Mild or minimally bothersome symptoms: watchful waiting with education, lifestyle advice (reduce evening fluids, caffeine and alcohol; double voiding; bladder training) and periodic review.

Bothersome moderate to severe LUTS: an alpha-blocker (tamsulosin, alfuzosin, silodosin, doxazosin or terazosin), chosen by age, comorbidity, blood pressure and ejaculatory side effects. Benefit appears within about 4 weeks.

Prostatic enlargement (volume over 30 g on imaging, PSA above 1.5 ng/mL or enlarged on DRE per AUA; over 40 mL per EAU): 5-ARI (finasteride or dutasteride) reduces progression, retention and surgery; judge effect after 6 to 12 months.
Moderate to severe LUTS with prostatic enlargement and risk of progression: combine an alpha-blocker with a 5-ARI.
Persistent storage symptoms: add an antimuscarinic or a beta-3 agonist (mirabegron). Avoid antimuscarinics if post-void residual is above 150 mL (EAU).
Tadalafil 5 mg daily treats LUTS with or without erectile dysfunction, alone or with an alpha-blocker or finasteride; never with nitrates.
Review 4 to 12 weeks after starting treatment (IPSS, and residual or flow if needed). If no improvement or side effects are intolerable, reassess, change treatment or refer.

sections.title: Acute urinary retention
items: Catheterise urethrally (suprapubic if urethral fails or is contraindicated); record the drained volume and check creatinine and electrolytes.
Start an alpha-blocker and continue it for at least 3 days before a trial without catheter (AUA).
Men who pass the trial remain at increased risk of recurrent retention: continue medication and arrange urology follow-up.
Chronic high-pressure retention with hydronephrosis or raised creatinine: catheterise, watch for post-obstructive diuresis (fluid and electrolyte monitoring) and refer for surgery.

sections.title: Surgery and referral
items: Surgery is indicated for refractory or recurrent retention, renal insufficiency or upper tract dilatation from obstruction, recurrent UTI, bladder stones, recurrent visible haematuria from the prostate, or LUTS not controlled by drugs.
Do not operate for an asymptomatic bladder diverticulum alone; assess for outlet obstruction.

Options: TURP (monopolar or bipolar) for 30 to 80 mL glands; laser enucleation (HoLEP, ThuLEP) at any size; photoselective vaporisation; simple prostatectomy for very large glands; incision (TUIP) for 30 g or less.
Minimally invasive options for 30 to 80 g glands: prostatic urethral lift or water vapour therapy (preserve ejaculation), robotic waterjet; prostatic artery embolisation by trained radiologists.
High bleeding risk (anticoagulants): HoLEP, ThuLEP or photoselective vaporisation are preferred.

sections.title: Drug cautions
items: Alpha-blockers: postural hypotension, dizziness and falls, especially in older men and with doxazosin or terazosin; ejaculatory dysfunction, especially with silodosin and tamsulosin.
Planned cataract surgery: warn about intraoperative floppy iris syndrome with alpha-blockers and ask him to tell the ophthalmologist.
5-ARIs lower PSA by about 50% after 6 months: double the measured PSA when monitoring for prostate cancer. Counsel about reduced libido, erectile and ejaculatory dysfunction.
Refractory prostatic haematuria after other causes are excluded: a 5-ARI may help (AUA).

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Blaming the prostate for all male LUTS: exclude UTI, stricture, stones, diabetes, heart failure or diuretics (nocturia), neurological disease and bladder cancer (haematuria).
Antimuscarinics in men with a large residual volume, risking retention.
Forgetting to double PSA in men on a 5-ARI and missing prostate cancer.
Using a 5-ARI in a small prostate, where it gives no benefit.

drugs.name: Tamsulosin
drugs.notes: Alpha-blocker. Postural hypotension, ejaculatory dysfunction, floppy iris syndrome.

drugs.name: Silodosin
drugs.dose: 8 mg orally once daily (4 mg in moderate renal impairment)

drugs.name: Doxazosin
drugs.dose: Start 1 mg orally once daily, titrate slowly to 4 to 8 mg daily
drugs.notes: Non-selective; greater first-dose and postural hypotension.

drugs.name: Finasteride
drugs.notes: 5-ARI for enlarged prostate. Halves PSA; sexual side effects.

drugs.name: Dutasteride
drugs.notes: 5-ARI for enlarged prostate. Halves PSA; sexual side effects.

drugs.name: Tadalafil
drugs.notes: LUTS with or without erectile dysfunction. Contraindicated with nitrates or nicorandil.

drugs.name: Mirabegron
drugs.dose: 50 mg orally once daily (25 mg in moderate renal or hepatic impairment)
drugs.notes: Storage symptoms. Check BP; avoid in severe uncontrolled hypertension.
